subject: Private deployment - evidence, deletion timelines, and attestation process

Subject: Private deployment - evidence and timelines for data deletion

Logan,

Thanks for the demo last week. We're finalizing procurement for a Private (VPC) deployment and need to confirm the exact deletion and attestation workflow before sign-off. A few specific questions: 

- If Acme Health requests a full data purge (production logs, customer payloads, model KV cache) from our VPC, what parts of that are executed by Redwood vs what we must execute in our cloud account?
- Are snapshots / EBS volumes created by Redwood agents? If so, who is the owner and how are they removed?
- What is the typical timeline from request to guaranteed removal and when can we expect a signed attestation?
- Can Redwood provide an artifact (logs, signed statement) that ties the deletion action to a specific request ID and timestamp?

We need this scoped for our Security & Compliance review. Appreciate a short bulleted response and any templates you can provide.

Best,
Liam
Senior IT Security, Acme Health

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary up front, then a proposed next step and attachments.

Short answers (high level):
- Control and ownership: In a Private/VPC deployment where storage (S3, EBS, managed DB) lives in Acme's cloud account, Acme is the ultimate owner of persisted snapshots/backups. Redwood runs agents and control-plane software that may create ephemeral caches and, in some configurations, orchestrate backups — but backups stored in your account remain under your control.
- What Redwood can guarantee: We can (a) execute deletion requests for any data our services have written to your resources upon documented request, (b) rotate and revoke any access credentials we hold, (c) purge local KV caches and model token caches on our side, and (d) produce a signed attestation and correlated operation logs showing the actions we took.
- Timeline: We initiate Redwood-side deletion actions within 24 hours of an approved request. Full completion for all Redwood-controlled artifacts (control-plane caches, temporary volumes, API logs) is typically within 72 hours. Final end-to-end evidence that all customer-account artifacts are removed depends on your cloud provider and any retained snapshots/lifecycle rules — often between 3–30 days.

Next step: I'm attaching our attestation template and a short VPC delete checklist. Priya and Karthik are on the thread to supply legal and technical clarifications. If you can tell us whether backups/snapshots are stored in Acme's account or a managed backup solution, we can give a precise SLA.

I'll follow up with a proposed DocuSign attestation once we align on wording.

Best,
Logan Wright
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Hi Liam — adding the legal perspective and specifics about attestations.

1) Statement of responsibility:
- If the storage is in Acme's cloud account (recommended for Private deployments), Acme controls snapshot lifecycle and object retention. Redwood's attestation will confirm actions executed by Redwood (control-plane/API calls, cache purges, credential revocations) but cannot assert deletion of objects that were never under Redwood's access control.

2) Attestation content we provide (typical):
- Request ID and timestamp (ISO8601) for the deletion request.
- List of Redwood-controlled artifacts removed (e.g., agent KV cache, ephemeral /tmp volumes on managed hosts, control-plane logs retained by Redwood).
- Actions taken to revoke access (keys rotated, tokens invalidated) with timestamps.
- Hash/digest of any exported evidence bundle (where applicable).
- Authorized Redwood signatory name, title, and digital signature (DocuSign).

3) Evidence we can include with attestation:
- Operation logs (agent uninstall/delete API calls), trimmed for PII.
- Control-plane audit trail showing the request lifecycle.
- If Acme shares read-only CloudTrail/Azure Activity logs or a pre-authorized temporary role, we can reference exact provider events in the attestation.

4) Timeline expectations:
- Redwood-side ops (initiate + complete): 24–72 hours.
- Attestation draft delivered: within 5 business days of completion.
- Final signed attestation: typically within 3 business days after sign-off (DocuSign).

If you'd like, we can pre-fill the attestation with Acme's legal contact details and route via DocuSign.

Regards,
Priya Natarajan
Head of Customer Trust & Legal, Redwood Inference

Hi all — technical checklist and notes to help your infra team validate deletion once a request is issued.

Technical checklist (Redwood-side vs Customer-side):
- Redwood-side (we will):
  * Revoke all Redwood service principals and API keys for the Acme deployment (rotate + delete), timestamped and logged.
  * Purge in-memory/model KV caches on all running agents (command: systemctl stop redwood-agent && /opt/redwood/bin/purge-kv --all).
  * Delete any ephemeral volumes created by Redwood-managed helpers and remove mountpoints.
  * Export operation logs and include a CRC-256 digest in the attestation.
- Customer-side (recommended steps for Acme):
  * Verify and delete S3 buckets/objects (aws s3 rm s3://acme-redwood-prod --recursive) and remove any lifecycle rules that keep versions.
  * Remove/terminate any snapshots (EBS) and confirm deletion in the EC2 console or via aws ec2 delete-snapshot --snapshot-id <id>.
  * If using managed DB snapshots, purge snapshot copies and replication targets.

Notes on snapshots/backups:
- Snapshots taken into Acme's account are owned by Acme; they persist according to Acme's snapshot policies. If you require immediate expiration of snapshots created before the request, Acme's infra team must delete them or grant Redwood a scoped role to do so.
- If Acme prefers, we can include a one-time, scoped runbook that allows Redwood to delete provider artifacts under a temporary IAM role — every action will be logged and included in the attestation.

Happy to hop on a short call with your infra lead to walk through the commands and the IAM scope.

—Karthik
Lead Infrastructure Security, Redwood Inference

Liam — attaching a short VPC delete playbook we typically share with customers. It maps each deletion item to the responsible party and shows expected timestamps for small (single-region) vs large (multi-region) deployments. High level:

- Redwood responsibilities (48–72 hours): revoke credentials, purge agent caches, uninstall agents on notification, export Redwood audit logs and evidence bundle.
- Customer responsibilities (1–30 days): remove provider snapshots/backups, clear blob/object storage, confirm deletion of replication targets.

Edge cases to call out:
- If any disaster recovery snapshots exist in a separate account or archive tier, those must be located and removed by the owner; Redwood's attestation will note if such artifacts were discovered but not removable by Redwood.
- Immutable backups retained by third-party backup vendors are outside Redwood's control; attestation will describe discovery and handoff steps.

Attachment: vpc-delete-checklist.xlsx
